description: Routing table of the build/general orchestrator. opencode-kit renders it into the build prompt (marker <!-- opencode-kit:routing -->) with only the rows of installed agents; a tie-breaker is shown only if every agent it names in backticks is installed.

rows.task: Creating/fixing a conda environment, dependency/solver conflicts, package installs
Nextflow/nf-core work with **no** more specific owner below — workflow/subworkflow logic, channel plumbing, `nextflow.config`, pipeline architecture, or a general nf-core question
Linting/validating an nf-core pipeline until it passes cleanly
Bioinformatics file-format code that must be correct (VCF/BAM/FASTA/GTF parsing, variant calling, omics stats)
Designing or writing a Python script, tool or package (structure, CLI, errors/logging, style, packaging, provenance), its pytest tests, black/ruff, porting R to Python
How to store data: choosing formats, config/secret layout, sample-sheet schemas, JSON-schema validation, state/backup/atomic writes, checksums/manifests, raw→normalized tables, output docs

An error, crash, or "why is this happening" question **outside** a Nextflow run

sections.heading: ### nf-core specialists — prefer these over `nextflow` when the request matches
sections.intro: Each owns a set of skills that encode the official nf-co.re procedure step by step. Routing to the specialist is strictly better than letting `nextflow` improvise the same procedure.

rows.task: Template sync, `TEMPLATE` branch, "template update for nf-core/tools vX" PR, pipeline is behind the template, scaffolding a new pipeline, `master`→`main` rename

A module or subworkflow: install, create, update, patch, deprecate, remove, wire into the workflow, `ext.args`, `conf/modules.config`, `environment.yml`, container/Wave URI, GPU module, private module remote, meta map / channel shape
nf-test, snapshots, "write/run tests", a failing pipeline run or crash in `work/`
Releasing a version, `bump-version`, release checklist, release PR, CHANGELOG for a release
README / `docs/usage.md` / `docs/output.md` / `CITATIONS.md` / CHANGELOG / MultiQC methods text after a pipeline change
Topic-channel migration, Nextflow strict syntax, institutional/HPC config profile

tie_breakers: A failing **Nextflow** run goes to `nf-core-testing` (it owns work-directory triage), not `debug-agent`. `debug-agent` keeps everything non-Nextflow.
Adding a tool to a pipeline is `nf-core-modules` (install *and* wire-in), not `nextflow`.
Changing a `params.*` and rebuilding the schema is `nf-core-modules`; the schema is never hand-edited by anyone.
Manuscript prose is `paper-writing`; pipeline documentation is `nf-core-docs`.

Python: structure/CLI/errors/packaging → `python-dev`; parsing or computing on VCF/BAM/FASTA/GTF content, where correctness of the genomics is the risk → `bioinformatics-agent`. A new `bin/` script that parses VCFs often needs both: `python-dev` for the script skeleton, then `bioinformatics-agent` for the record logic.

Tests: *what* to test and with which data → `test-design` (plans, use cases, synthetic data, failure cases); nf-test mechanics and snapshots → `nf-core-testing`; SEQC2/GIAB datasets → `refdata` (if installed). Order: `test-design` → (`refdata`) → implementer.
A new file format, config, schema or storage decision → `data-formats` first, then the implementer.
If two specialists both fit, run them in sequence in the natural order (design → implement → test → document), not in parallel on the same files.
If none fits, `nextflow` is the fallback for anything Nextflow-related.
